newsitem.title: GERMANY: Palestinian hijacker gets 12 years in German jail.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian hijacker gets 12 years in German jail.

text.p: The only survivor of four Palestinians who seized a Lufthansa jet in 1977 and killed the pilot to back demands by German Red Army Faction guerrillas was jailed for 12 years by a Hamburg court on Tuesday.

Souhaila Andrawes, 42, was convicted for the murder of captain Juergen Schumann who was shot at Mogadishu airport in Somalia. She was also charged with hijacking, kidnapping, hostage-taking and attempted murder.

Andrawes had been convicted in Somalia for the hijacking and sentenced to 20 years in jail, but was released after a year and went home to Beirut. She moved to Norway in 1991 and was extradited to Germany four years later.
The hijackers were backing demands by German RAF guerrillas for the release of 11 of its members from jail.
Prosecutor Volker Homann said the four hijackers had decided together to shoot captain Schumann and Andrawes was held responsible though she did not pull the trigger herself.
She had admitted taking part in the hijack, but denied any responsibility for the captain's murder.
The hostage drama ended after five days when German GSG-9 commandos stormed the aircraft at Mogadishu airport, killing three of the hijackers and freeing 86 passengers.
Homann said the court would take into account time Andrawes had spent in prison in Mogadishu and Norway. He said she was likely to serve three years and ten months in Germany.
